chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Yunus, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I intended to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so I put on my clothes and spread out a new pallium (cloak) that I was fond of. A camel squeezed me on one of the paths, so it tore from every side, and I was saddened by that.
So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he looked at the pallium and said to me: 'What is the matter? I see you as torn.' So I informed him of the story.

So he said: 'O Umar! When you wear a new garment, say: 'There is no god except Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' you will be free from misfortune. And when you love something, do not mention it frequently, for that is from what crushes you. And if you have a need from a man, do not insult him from behind (in his absence), for Allah will place that in his heart.'

key_terms.طَيْلَسَان: A type of cloak or pallium worn in ancient times
key_terms.مِنْ خَلْفِهِ: From behind him (i.e., in his absence/backbiting)
key_terms.يَهُدُّكَ: Crushes you or diminishes your status/blessing

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes and supplications when wearing new clothes according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches Umar ibn Yazeed the spiritual etiquette of wearing new garments, linking the recitation of the Shahada to protection from *al-afah* (divine affliction or the evil eye). The Imam further connects material attachment and interpersonal dynamics to spiritual well-being, advising against excessive mention of beloved things to prevent spiritual depletion and avoiding backbiting to ensure one's needs are met, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a means of divine favor.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Husayn Al Neyshapouri, form Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan, from Yunus, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I wanted to go over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I wore my clothes and displayed my new pallium which I was fascinated with. So a camel squeezed me in one of the streets, so it ruptured from every direction. Thus I was gloomy due to that.

So I came over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> looked at my pallium, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘What is the matter I<sup>asws</sup> see you with torn clothes?’ So I informed him with the story.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Umar! Whenever you wear new clothes, so say, ‘There is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’, you would be free from the misfortunes; and whenever you love something so do not mention it frequently, for that is from what crushes you; and whenever there is a need for you to a man, so do not insult him from his behind, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Make that to occur in his heart’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburiy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Rayyan from Yunus from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following:

“I once wanted to visit abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. I dressed up and spread my Taylisan (pallium) which was new and I liked it very much. Somewhere on the road the camel gave me a hard time and it (my dress) was torn in pieces all over. I became depress very much.
I then met abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, he looked at my Taylisan and asked, ‘Why do I see your cloth ripped apart?’ I then informed him (the Imam) about what had happened.

He (the Imam) said, ‘O ‘Umar, whenever you will wear a new pair of clothes say, “No one deserves worship except Allah. Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.’ You will remain safe from misfortunes and if you like something do not mention it very often because mentioning it causes you great damage. If you need something from a person do not revile him behind his back because Allah drops it in his heart.’”
